verdict.rationale: CrewAI's core is described as an open-source framework that users install and run locally (uv tool install crewai), with a public GitHub repository. However, the production layer (CrewAI AMP: managed deployment, Crew Studio, Visual Builders, Tool Repository, REST API access) is documented only as managed infrastructure. Self-hosting therefore covers the framework but not the full platform, and the evidence never explicitly addresses self-hosting, licensing, or deploying to your own servers. missing for 10: explicit self-hosting or deployment documentation for your own infrastructure, a stated open-source license, a self-hostable version of the AMP features (deployment, Studio, REST API, webhooks), and independent hands-on corroboration of self-hosted production use

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: CrewAI AMP extends the power of the open-source framework with features designed for production deployments, collaboration, and scalability.
It gives developers autonomous agent collaboration through Crews and precise, event-driven control through Flows.
Deploy your crews to a managed infrastructure with a few clicks
